issue.title: bob highlights clip: --from-chrome Mac capture and a Bob Mac Capture/Shortcuts entry point

task_type_fields.proposal:
Add a Mac-native entry point for `bob highlights clip` (proposed by phase bob-cli-35.5 of epic bob-cli-35, recorded by bob-cli-35.land):

- `bob highlights clip --from-chrome` on macOS: capture the article from the frontmost Google Chrome tab (the page Bryan is already reading, already past any bot wall or login), instead of launching a fresh automated browser. It would feed the existing `--html` replay path (adapter protocol v1, `capture.mode: html-file`) with the tab's URL and saved DOM.
- A Bob Mac Capture (bob-mac-capture repo) or macOS Shortcuts action that spawns `bob highlights clip <URL>` for the current tab and shows the `ok`/`error:`/`hint:` result. Per decision `mac-capture-is-a-thin-client`, the Mac app must only run bob and render what it returns; it never parses or renders the article itself.

Context: `bob highlights clip` landed in epic bob-cli-35 (commits fd12809, e355016, 44bfe58, 5c6e2ad, a35b255; contract in docs/highlights-clip.md). Today a Mac user must run the CLI by hand, and bot-protected sites need headed Chrome (athena under Xvfb) or a manual Save Page As + `--html FILE`.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: The approved epic plan plan:202610/web_url_highlights_clip.md lists `--from-chrome` and a Mac entry point under "Out of scope", and epic bob-cli-35 delivered only the Linux-verified CLI. This work spans bob-cli and bob-mac-capture (a capture-contract change across both repos) and needs its own plan.

issue.creation_reason: Epic bob-cli-35's live-verify phase proposed a Mac-native clip entry point as a follow-up; the epic plan explicitly left --from-chrome and Mac/Shortcuts integration out of scope.
